column2: As for the western portion of the section, a mountain cuts across it, beginning from the mountain of the non-Arabs and running east to the end of the section; it is called the mountain of Shahrazūr, and it divides this portion into two portions. In the south of this small portion is the town of Khūnjān, to the west and north of Isfahan, and this portion is called the land of al-Halūs; in the middle of it is the town of Nihāwand, and in its north the town of Shahrazūr, in the west, at the meeting point of the two mountains, and al-Dīnawar in the east, at the end of the section. In the second small portion is [a part] of the land of Armenia, whose capital is al-Marāgha; the part of the mountain of Iraq that faces it is called Bāriyā, and it is the dwelling place of the Kurds, and the Greater and Lesser Zāb, which is on the Tigris, lies behind it. At the end of this portion, on the east side, is the land of Azerbaijan, which includes Tabriz and al-Baydaqān. In the north-eastern corner of this section is a portion of the Sea of Nīṭish (the Black Sea), which is the Sea of the Khazars. In the seventh section of this zone, in its west and south, is most of the land of al-Halūs, in which are Hamadan and Qazvin; the rest of it is in the third zone, and in it there is Isfahan. A mountain surrounds it on the south, issuing from its west and passing through the third zone, then bending from the sixth section into the fourth zone and joining the mountain of Iraq in its east, which was mentioned there; and it encloses the land of al-Halūs in the eastern portion

and this mountain that surrounds Isfahan descends from the third zone toward the north and comes out into this seventh section, and encloses the land of al-Halūs on its east; beneath it there lie Kāshān and then Qum. Near the middle of its course it bends somewhat to the west, then returns, curving round, and goes east, veering to the north, until it comes out into the fifth zone, and in its bend and curve it takes in the town of al-Rayy on its east side. And from its bend another mountain begins, which passes west to the end of this section; to the south of it there lies Qazvin. And on its northern side, and the side of the mountain of al-Rayy joined with it, going east and north to the middle of the section and then into the fifth zone, lies the land of Ṭabaristān, between these mountains and a portion of the Sea of Ṭabaristān (the Caspian Sea), and it enters this section from the fifth zone over about half of it, from its west to its east. And a mountain joined to it cuts across at the mountain of al-Rayy, at its bend to the west, running in its line to the east with a slight veering to the south, until it enters the eighth section from its west; and between the mountain of al-Rayy and this mountain, from where they begin, there remains the land of Jurjān, between the two mountains, and Basṭām is in it. And beyond this mountain is a portion of this section in which is the rest of the desert between Fārs and Khurāsān; it is east of Kāshān

and at its end, by this mountain, is the town of Astarābādh; and the flanks of this mountain, from its east to the end of the section, are the land of Nishapur, in Khurāsān. South of the mountain and east of the desert is the town of Nishapur, then Marw al-Shāhjān at the end of the section; and north of it and east of Jurjān are the towns of Mihrajān and Khāzarūn, and Ṭūs at the end of the section in the east. All this is below the mountain. And north of these is the land of Nasā, and around it, at the corner of the two parts, north and east, are uninhabited deserts. In the eighth section of this zone, in its west, is the river Jayḥūn, going from south to north. On its western bank are Ramm and Āmul, of the land of Khurāsān, and al-Ẓāhiriyya and al-Jurjāniyya, of the land of Khwārazm. The south-western corner of it is surrounded by the mountain of Astarābādh, which cuts across the seventh section before it and comes out in this section from its west and surrounds this corner, in which lies the rest of the land of Herat and al-Jūzjān, until it joins the mountain of al-Butm, as we mentioned there. In the east of the river Jayḥūn in this section, and in the south of it, are the land of Bukhara, then the land of Sughd, whose capital is Samarkand, then Surdārā and Ushna, and among them is Khujanda, at the end of the section in the east. And to the north of Samarkand

and Surdār and Ushna, the land of Īlāq; then, north of Īlāq, the land of al-Shāsh to the end of the section in the east, and it takes a portion of the ninth section, and in the south of that portion lies the rest of the land of Farghāna. And from that portion in the ninth section the river of al-Shāsh comes out, passing across the eighth section until it pours into the Jayḥūn where the latter leaves this eighth section, on its north, for the fifth zone. And there joins it, in the land of Īlāq, a river that comes from the ninth section of the third zone, from the borders of the land of Tibet, and before it leaves the ninth section the river of Farghāna joins it. And in the line of the river of al-Shāsh is the mountain of Jabrāghūn, which begins in the fifth zone and bends east, veering to the south, until it comes out into the ninth section, enclosing the land of al-Shāsh; then it bends in the ninth section and encloses al-Shāsh and Farghāna there, to its south, and enters the third zone. Between the river of al-Shāsh and the end of this mountain, in the middle of this section, is the land of Fārāb, and between it and the land of Bukhara and Khwārazm are uninhabited deserts. And in the corner of this section, at the north and east, is the land of Khujanda, in which are the towns of Isbījāb and Ṭarāz.

And in the ninth section of this zone, in its west, beyond the land of Farghāna and al-Shāsh, is the land of al-Khazlajiyya in the south and the land of al-Khalīja in the north; and in the east of the whole section is the land of al-Kīmākiyya, which continues through the whole of the tenth section to Mount Qūqiyā, at the end of the section in the east, and on a portion of the Encircling Ocean there; it is the mountain of Gog and Magog. All these nations are of the Turkish peoples. Here it ends.
The fifth zone:

The first section of it is mostly covered with water, except for a little of its south and east, because the Encircling Ocean on this western side has entered the fifth, sixth and seventh zones, away from the circle that surrounds the zone. As for what is uncovered of its south, it is a portion in the shape of a triangle, connected there with al-Andalus, the rest of which lies on it, and the sea surrounds it from two sides, as though they were two sides enclosing the angle of the triangle. In it, of the rest of the west of al-Andalus, are Saʿyūr, on the sea, at the beginning of the section from the south and west, and Salamanca to the east of it, and in its interior Zamora; and east of Salamanca is Ayla, at the end of the south, and the land of Castile to the east of it, in which is the city of Segovia; and in the north of it are the land of León and Burgos, and then behind it in the north the land of Galicia, up to the corner of the portion, in which, on the Encircling Ocean, at the end of the western side, is the town of Shanniyāqū, which means Yaʿqūb. And in it, of the east of the land of al-Andalus, is the city of Shaṭliya, at the end of the section in the south, east of Castile; and in its north and east are Huesca and Pamplona, in its line, to the east and north, and west of Pamplona is Qashtāla, then Nājiza, between it and Burgos. And a great mountain cuts across the middle of this portion, parallel to the sea and to the north-eastern side of it, and nearby, and it is joined to it

and to the end of the sea at Pamplona on the east side, which we mentioned before is joined in the south to the Mediterranean in the fourth zone, and becomes a barrier around the land of al-Andalus from the east; and its passes have gates leading to the land of Gascony, of the Frankish nations. Of them, from the fourth zone, are Barcelona and Narbonne, on the coast of the Mediterranean, and Kharīda and Carcassonne behind them in the north; and of them, from the fifth zone, is Toulouse, north of Kharīda. As for what is uncovered in this section on the east side, it is a portion in the shape of an elongated triangle, with its acute angle beyond the Pyrenees to the east; and in it, on the Encircling Ocean, at the head of the portion to which the mountain of the Pyrenees is joined, is the town of Niyūna. And at the end of this portion, in the north-eastern part of the section, is the land of Banṭū, of the Franks, to the end of the section.

And in the second section, in its western part, is the land of Gascony, and in the north of it the land of Banṭū and Burgos, which we have mentioned. And east of the land of Gascony, in the north of it, a portion of the Mediterranean has entered this section like a molar, inclining a little to the east, and the land of Gascony lies to the west of it, jutting into an inlet of the sea. At the head of this portion, in the north, is the land of Genoa, and in line with it in the north Mount Nīt Jūn, and in the north of that, in its line, the land of Burgundy. East of the arm of Genoa that issues from the Mediterranean there is another arm issuing from it, leaving between them an inlet that enters from the land into the sea, in the west of which is Nīsh, and in its east the great city of Rome, the seat of the kingship of the Franks and the residence of the pope, their supreme patriarch. In it are such huge buildings, awesome temples and ancient churches that the reports of them are well known; and among its wonders is the river that flows through the middle of it from east to west, its bed paved with slabs of copper. In it is the church of Peter and Paul, two of the Apostles, who are buried there. And north of the land of Rome is the land of Aqranṣīṣa, to the end of the section,

and on this arm of the sea, in the south of which is Rome, is the land of Naples, on its eastern side, adjoining the land of Calabria, of the lands of the Franks; and in the north of it an arm of the Gulf of the Venetians has entered this section from the third section, going west and parallel to the north of this section, and has reached about a third of it; and on it are many of the lands of the Venetians, extending into this section from its south, between it and the Encircling Ocean; and to the north of it is the land of Inkilāya, in the sixth zone. And in the third section of this zone, in its west, is the land of Calabria, between the Gulf of the Venetians and the Mediterranean, which surrounds it on its east; it extends from its mainland in the fourth zone into the Mediterranean, in an inlet between two arms that issued from the sea in the direction of the north into this section. East of the land of Calabria is the land of Ankubarda, in an inlet between the Gulf of the Venetians and the Mediterranean, and a tip of this section enters the inlet in the fourth zone and the Mediterranean, and the Gulf of the Venetians, from the Mediterranean, surrounds it on its east, going in the direction of the north, then bends to the west, parallel to the northern end of the section

and a great mountain comes out in its line from the fourth zone, running parallel to it and going with it to the north, then turning west with it in the sixth zone until it ends opposite a gulf, to the north of it, in the land of Inkilāya, of the German nations, as we shall mention. And on this gulf, and between it and this mountain, so long as the two go northward, are the lands of the Venetians; and when they go west, between them are the land of Ḥarwāya and then the land of the Germans, at the end of the gulf. And in the fourth section of this zone is a portion of the Mediterranean that came out into it from the fourth zone, toothed all over with portions of the sea, which go out from it to the north; and between each two teeth of it is an arm of the sea in the inlet between them. And at the end of the section, in the east, are portions of the sea, and out of them to the north goes the Gulf of Constantinople. It comes out of this southern arm and goes in the direction of the north; the Gulf of Constantinople comes out of this southern arm and goes in the direction of the north until it enters the sixth zone, and from there, shortly after, it bends east to the Sea of Nīṭish in the fifth section and part of the fourth before it

and the sixth after it, of the sixth zone, as we shall mention. And the town of Constantinople is east of this gulf, at the end of the section in the north; it is the great city that was the seat of the Caesars, and it has such remains of building and vastness that many tales have been told of them. And the portion of this section that lies between the Mediterranean and the Gulf of Constantinople includes the land of Macedonia, which belonged to the Greeks, and from which their kingship began. And east of this gulf, to the end of the section, is a portion of the land of Bāṭūs, which I think at the present time is the roaming grounds of the Turkmen; the kingship of Ibn ʿUthmān is in it, and his capital there is Bursa. Before them it belonged to the Rūm, and the nations overcame them there until it passed to the Turkmen. And in the fifth section of this zone, in its west and south, is the land of Bāṭūs, and north of it to the end of the section the land of ʿAmmūriya, and east of ʿAmmūriya the river Qabāqib, which feeds the Euphrates; it comes out of a mountain there and goes south until it mingles with the Euphrates before the latter passes from this section to its course in the fourth zone. And there in the west of it, at the end of the section, is the source of the river Sayḥān, then the river Jayḥān to the west of it, both going in its line; they have been mentioned before. And in its east there is the source of the Tigris, which goes in its line and parallel to it until it meets it at Baghdad. And in the corner between the south and the east of this section

beyond the mountain from which the Tigris begins is the town of Mayyāfāriqīn. And the river Qabāqib that we mentioned divides this section into two portions, one of them western and southern, in which is the land of Bāṭūs, as we have said, and its lower parts to the end of the section in the north; and beyond the mountain from which the river Qabāqib begins is the land of ʿAmmūriya, as we have said. The second portion is eastern and northern, taking up a third [of the section]; in the south of it is the source of the Tigris and the Euphrates, and in the north the land of al-Baylaqān, adjoining the land of ʿAmmūriya from beyond the mountain of Qabāqib; it is broad, and at its end, at the source of the Euphrates, is the town of Kharshana. In the north-eastern corner is a portion of the Sea of Nīṭish, which the Gulf of Constantinople feeds.

And in the sixth section of this zone, in its south and west, is the land of Armenia, continuing until it passes the middle of the section toward the east side; in it are towns: Ardan in the south and west, and in the north of it Tiflīs and Dabīl; east of Ardan is the city of Khilāṭ, then Bardhaʿa; in the south of it, inclining to the east, is the city of Arminiya, and from there the land of Armenia goes out into the fourth zone. And there in it is the town of al-Marāgha, east of the mountain of the Kurds called Armā, which was mentioned in the sixth section of the fourth zone. And adjoining the land of Armenia, in this section and in the fourth zone before it, on the east side, is [a region] in which lies the land of Azerbaijan, and its end in this section, to the east, is the land of Ardabīl, on a portion of the Sea of Ṭabaristān that has entered the eastern part of the seventh section, and it is called the Sea of Ṭabaristān; and on it, to the north of it in this section, is a portion of the land of the Khazars, who are the Turkmen. And from the end of this part of the sea in the north there begin mountains joined to one another in the direction of the west up to the fifth section, and they pass through it, bending and surrounding the town of Mayyāfāriqīn, and it goes out into the fourth zone at Āmid and joins the Chain Mountain in the lower parts of Syria, and from there it joins Mount Lukkām, as was mentioned. And between these northern mountains in this section are passes like gateways, leading from the two sides

and in the south of them is the land of al-Abwāb, extending in the east to the Sea of Ṭabaristān, and on it, of this land, is the city of Bāb al-Abwāb; and the land of al-Abwāb joins, in the west, on its southern side, the land of Armenia, and between the two of them in the east, and the southern land of Azerbaijan, is the land of al-Zāb, extending to the Sea of Ṭabaristān. And north of these mountains is a portion of this section, in the west of which is the kingdom of al-Sarīr, in its north-western corner; and in the corner of the whole section is also a portion of the Sea of Nīṭish, which the Gulf of Constantinople feeds, and which has been mentioned. The land of al-Sarīr borders this portion of Nīṭish, and on it, of that land, is the town of Aṭrābazīda Bazīda; and the land of al-Sarīr extends between the mountain of al-Abwāb and the northern side of the section until it ends in the east at a barrier mountain between it and the land of the Khazars, and at its end is the city of Ṣūl. And beyond this barrier mountain is a portion of the land of the Khazars, which ends at the north-eastern corner of this section, at the Sea of Ṭabaristān and the end of the section in the north.

And the seventh section of this zone has its west entirely covered by the Sea of Ṭabaristān, and from its south, in the fourth zone, there emerged the portion on which, as we mentioned there, are the land of Ṭabaristān and the mountains of al-Daylam as far as Qazvin. And in the west of that portion, joined to it, is the portion that is in the sixth section of the fourth zone, and joined to it on its north is the portion that is in the sixth section, in the east of it also. And a portion of this section is uncovered at its north-western corner, into which the river Athil pours into this sea. And there remains in the east of this section a portion uncovered by the sea, which is the roaming grounds of the Ghuzz, of the Turkish nations. A mountain surrounds it on the south, entering the eighth section and going west to a point short of its middle, then it bends to the north until it meets the Sea of Ṭabaristān and skirts it, going with it to the rest of it in the sixth zone; then it bends with its end and leaves it, and is called there Mount Siyāh, and goes west to the sixth section of the sixth zone, then returns south to the sixth section of the fifth zone. And this end of it is the one that cut across, in this section, between the land of al-Sarīr and the land of the Khazars, and the sides of this mountain, called Mount Siyāh, join with the land of the Khazars in the sixth and seventh sections, as will come.

And the eighth section of this fifth zone is entirely roaming grounds of the Ghuzz, of the Turkish nations. In its south-western part is the Lake of Khwārazm, into which the Jayḥūn pours; its circumference is 300 miles, and many rivers from the land of these roaming grounds pour into it. In its north-eastern part is Lake ʿArʿūn, whose circumference is 400 miles and whose water is sweet. In the northern part of this section is Mount Murghār, which means the mountain of snow, because the snow does not melt on it; it joins the end of the section. South of Lake ʿArʿūn is a mountain of hard rock that grows nothing, called ʿArʿūn, and the lake is named after it; and from it and from Mount Murghār, north of the lake, flow rivers beyond counting, which pour into it from the two sides. And in the ninth section of this zone is the land of Arkas, of the Turkish nations, west of the land of the Ghuzz and east of the land of al-Kīmākiyya; and it is bordered on its east side, at the end of the section, by Mount Qūqiyā, which encircles Gog and Magog. It cuts across there from south to north until it bends where it first enters from the tenth section, having entered it from the end of the tenth section of the fourth zone before it, and there skirted the Encircling Ocean to the end of the section in the north, then bent west in the tenth section of the fourth zone to a point short of its half

and it enclosed, from its beginning to here, the land of al-Kīmākiyya, then came out into the tenth section of the fifth zone and went in it west to its end, and there remained in the south of it, of this section, a portion extending to the west before the end of the land of al-Kīmākiyya; then it came out into the ninth section on its east, in the upper part of it, and bent soon to the north and went in its line to the ninth section of the sixth zone, where the Barrier is, as we shall mention. And there remained of it the portion that Mount Qūqiyā encloses at the north-eastern corner of this section, extending to the south, and it is part of the land of Gog and Magog. And in the tenth section of this zone the land of Gog and Magog is continuous throughout it, except for a portion of the sea that has covered a strip on its east, from its south to its north, and except for the portion that Mount Qūqiyā separates off to the south and west as it passes through it; everything other than that is the land of Gog and Magog. And God, glory be to Him, the Exalted, knows best.
The sixth zone.

As for the first section of it, the sea has covered more than half of it, and has curved east along the northern side, then gone south along the eastern side and ended near the southern side; so a portion of this land is uncovered in this section, entering between the two arms and in the south-eastern corner of the Encircling Ocean, like an inlet in it, and it widens in length and breadth; the whole of it is the land of Brīṭāniya. And at its gate, between the two arms, in the south-eastern corner of this section, is the land of Ṣāqis, adjoining the land of Banṭū, which was mentioned in the first and second sections of the fifth zone. And the second section of this zone has been entered by the Encircling Ocean from its west and its north. From its west comes an elongated portion, larger than its northern half, from the east of the land of Brīṭāniya in the first section, and the other portion in the north joined it, from its west to its east, and widened somewhat in its western half; and in it there is a portion of the island of England, a great island containing cities, in which there is a mighty kingship, and the rest of it is in
the seventh zone

And south of this portion and its island, in the western half of this section, are the land of Normandy and the land of Flanders, joined to it, then the land of France in the south and west of this section, and the land of Burgundy to the east of it; all of them belong to the Frankish nations. And the land of the Germans is in the eastern half of the section: in its south the land of Inkilāya, then the land of Burgundy to the north, then the land of Lahwīka and Shaṭūniya, and on the portion of the Encircling Ocean in the north-eastern corner the land of Afrīra; all of them belong to the German nations. And in the third section of this zone, in the western part, are the land of Marātiya in the south and the land of Shaṭūniya in the north, and in the eastern part the land of Ankuwiya in the south and the land of Bulūniya in the north, with Mount Balwāṭ cutting across between them, entering from the fourth section and passing west, veering to the north, until it stops in the land of Shaṭūniya at the end of the western half. And in the fourth section, in the southern part, is the land of Jathūliya, and below it in the north the land of the Rus, and Mount Balwāṭ separates them from the beginning of the section in the west until it stops in the eastern half; and east of the land of Jathūliya is the land of Jirmāniya, and in the south-eastern corner the land of Constantinople, whose city is at the end of the gulf that issues from the Mediterranean, at its outlet into the Sea of Nīṭish, so that a small portion of the Sea of Nīṭish falls in the upper part of the eastern side of this section, and the gulf feeds it, and between them, in the corner, is the town of Masīnāh.

And in the fifth section of the sixth zone, then in the southern part, at the Sea of Nīṭish, it connects with the gulf at the end of the fourth section and issues in its line eastward, and passes through all of this section and part of the sixth, over a length of 1,300 miles from its beginning, with a breadth of 600 miles. And there remains beyond this sea, in the southern part of this section, from its west to its east, an elongated stretch of land; in its west is Heraclea, on the coast of the Sea of Nīṭish, adjoining the land of al-Baylaqān of the fifth zone, and in its east the land of al-Lāniya, whose capital is Sūtlī, on the Sea of Nīṭish. And in the north of the Sea of Nīṭish in this section, in the west, is the land of Tarkhān, and in the east the land of the Rus, all of them on the coast of this sea. And the land of the Rus surrounds the land of Tarkhān on its east, in this section, on its north, in the fifth section of the seventh zone, and on its west, in the fourth section of this zone.

And in the sixth section, in its west, is the remainder of the Sea of Nīṭish, which veers a little to the north; and there remains between it there and the end of the section in the north the land of Qumāniya. And south of it, widening toward the north in proportion to its veering, is the rest of the land of al-Lāniya, which had been at the end of its south in the fifth section. And in the eastern part of this section, continuous, is the land of the Khazars, and east of it the land of Burṭās, and in the north-eastern corner the land of Bulghār, and in the south-eastern corner the land of Baljar, which a portion of Mount Siyākūh crosses there, the mountain that bends with the Sea of the Khazars in the seventh section after it and, after leaving it, goes west and crosses this portion and enters the sixth section of the fifth zone, where it joins the mountain of al-Abwāb; and on it, from there, lies the district of the land of the Khazars. And in the seventh section of this zone, in the southern part, is the land that Mount Siyāh crosses after leaving the Sea of Ṭabaristān, a portion of the land of the Khazars, to the end of the section in the west; and in the east of it is the portion of the Sea of Ṭabaristān that this mountain skirts on its east and north; and beyond Mount Siyāh, in the north-western part, is the land of Burṭās, and in the eastern part of the section the land of Shaḥrab and Yakhnāk, who are Turkish nations.

And in the eighth section, the whole of the southern part of it is the land of al-Jūlakh, of the Turks; in the northern part, in the west, [is] the Stinking Land, and the east of the land which, it is said, Gog and Magog laid waste before the building of the Barrier. In this Stinking Land is the source of the river Athil, one of the greatest rivers of the world; its course is in the land of the Turks and its mouth is in the Sea of Ṭabaristān, in the fifth zone, in the seventh section of it. It has many bends. It comes out of a mountain in the Stinking Land from three springs that unite in one river, and passes in the direction of the west to the end of the seventh section of this zone, then bends north to the seventh section of the seventh zone and passes through its edge between the south and the west, and comes out in the sixth section of the seventh, and goes west not far, then bends a second time to the south and returns to the sixth section of the sixth zone, and a stream comes out of it, going west and pouring into the Sea of Nīṭish in that section, while it itself passes through a portion between the north and the east in the land of Bulghār, and comes out in the seventh section of the sixth zone, then bends a third time to the south and pierces Mount Siyāh and passes through the land of the Khazars and comes out into the fifth zone in the seventh section of it, and there pours into the Sea of Ṭabaristān in the portion that was uncovered of the section at the south-western corner.

As for the ninth section of this zone, in its western side is the land of Khafshākh, of the Turks, who are the Qifjāq, and the land of the Circassians, also of them; and in the east of it is the land of Gog, the two being separated by the encircling Mount Qūqiyā, which has been mentioned. It begins from the Encircling Ocean in the east of the fourth zone and goes with it to the end of the zone in the north, and leaves it going west and veering to the north until it enters the ninth section of the fifth zone, then returns to its first line until it enters this ninth section of the zone from its south to its north, veering to the west; and in its middle here is the Barrier that Alexander built. Then it goes on in its line into the seventh zone, in the ninth section of it, and passes through it to the south until it meets the Encircling Ocean in its north; then it bends with it from there west into the seventh zone, to the fifth section of it, where it joins a portion of the Encircling Ocean in its west. And in the middle of this ninth section is the Barrier that Alexander built, as we have said, and the sound report of it is in the Qurʾān. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khurradādhbih mentioned in his book on geography that al-Wāthiq saw in his sleep as though the Barrier had opened, and he awoke in alarm and sent Sallām the interpreter, who came upon it and brought back its report and its description, in a long story that is not among the purposes of this book of ours. And in the tenth section of this zone is the land of Magog, continuous in it to its end, on a portion of the Encircling Ocean there, which surrounds it on its east and north, elongated in the north and somewhat broad in the east.
The seventh zone:

And the Encircling Ocean has covered most of it, from the north up to the middle of the fifth section, where it joins Mount Qūqiyā, which encircles Gog and Magog. The first and second sections are covered with water, except what is uncovered of the island of England, most of which is in the second, while in the first there is an arm of it that bends, veering to the north; and the rest of it, with a portion of the sea curving round it, is in the second section of the sixth zone, and it is mentioned there; and the crossing from it to the mainland in this portion is twelve miles wide. And beyond this island, in the north of the second section, is the island of Raslānda, elongated from west to east. And the third section of this zone is mostly covered by the sea, except an elongated portion in its south that widens in its east; in it, there, continuous, is the land of Fulūniya, which was mentioned in the third section of the sixth zone, and that it is in the north of it. And in the portion of the sea that covers this section, then in the western side of it, it is round and spacious, and it joins the mainland by a gate in its south leading to the land of Fulūniya, and in the north of it is the island of Barʿāqiba (in one manuscript, Būqāʿa), elongated along the north from west to east.

And the fourth section of this zone has its north entirely covered by the Encircling Ocean from west to east, and its south uncovered; in its west is the land of Qaymāzak, of the Turks, and east of it the land of Ṭast, then the land of Raslān, to the end of the section in the east; it is always snowy and its settlement is slight, and it adjoins the land of the Rus in the sixth zone, in the fourth and fifth sections of it. And in the fifth section of this zone, in the western part of it, is the land of the Rus, and it ends in the north at a portion of the Encircling Ocean to which Mount Qūqiyā is joined, as we mentioned before; and in the eastern part of it, continuous, is the land of Qumāniya, which lies on the portion of the Sea of Nīṭish in the sixth section of the sixth zone, and it ends at Lake Ṭarmā in this section, which is fresh, and many rivers from the mountains to the south and north flow into it. And in the north of the eastern part of this section is the land of the Tatars, of the Turks (in one manuscript, the Turkmen), to its end.

And in the sixth section, in the south-western part, continuous, is the land of Qumāniya, and in the middle of this part is Lake ʿUthūr, fresh, into which rivers flow from the mountains in the eastern parts; it is always frozen on account of the intense cold, except for a little in the summer season. And east of the land of Qumāniya is the land of the Rus, which began in the sixth zone, in the north-eastern part of the fifth section of it; and in the south-eastern corner of this section is the rest of the land of Bulghār, which began in the sixth zone, in the north-eastern part of the sixth section of it; and in the middle of this portion of the land of Bulghār is the bend of the river Athil, the first portion, to the south, as was mentioned. And at the end of this sixth section, on its north, is Mount Qūqiyā, continuous from its west to its east. And in the seventh section of this zone, in its west, is the rest of the land of Yakhnāk, of the Turkish nations, which began in the north-eastern part of the sixth section before it; and in the south-western part of this section, and it goes out into the sixth zone from above it; and in the eastern part is the rest of the land of Saḥrab, then the rest of the Stinking Land to the end of the section in the east; and at the end of the section on the north side is the encircling Mount Qūqiyā, continuous from its west to its east.

And in the eighth section of this zone, in the south-western part of it, is the Stinking Land, continuous, and in the east of it the Excavated Land, which is one of the wonders: a vast rent in the earth, deep in its fall, wide in its expanses, its bottom impossible to reach; that it is inhabited is inferred from the smoke by day and the fires by night, which shine and vanish, and sometimes a river is seen in it, cutting through it from south to north. And in the eastern part of this section are the ruined lands adjoining the Barrier, and at the end of the north of it is Mount Qūqiyā, continuous from east to west. And in the ninth section of this zone, in its western side, is the land of Khafshākh, who are the Qifjaq; Mount Qūqiyā passes through it when it bends from its north at the Encircling Ocean and goes in its middle to the south, veering to the east, and comes out in the ninth section of the sixth zone and passes across it, and in its middle there is the Barrier of Gog and Magog, which we have mentioned. And in the eastern part of this section is the land of Gog, beyond Mount Qūqiyā, on the sea, narrow in breadth and elongated, which surrounds it on its east and north. The sea has covered the tenth section entirely. This is the end of the discussion of geography and its seven zones. “In the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day there are signs for all creatures.”
